purpose: Independent source-only collation of the complete fifteen-star plant roster for the planned GDT960 source models

source.title: Three Books of Occult Philosophy, Book I, Chapter XXXII: What things are under the Signes, the fixed Stars, and their Images
source.attribution: Henry Cornelius Agrippa; English witness/transmission attributed to him
source.witness_chronology: The EEBO item is a 1651 English translation witness. The Wikisource page is a transcription of the same early-modern English text. Agrippa's work has earlier sixteenth-century print history, but this collation does not establish that every plant row or spelling was unchanged from a medieval source.
source.source_loci: Wikisource chapter paragraphs 104-110: the fifteen numbered stars begin with the head of Algol and end with the Tail of Capricorn; the following paragraph states the conjoined-influence qualification.
source.access_limit: Source text only; no Voynich target, target scoring, image, reserve, or new manuscript data was opened.

scope.included: The numbered fixed-star rows and their plant entries.
scope.excluded_from_roster: The chapter first lists sign-associated and planet-associated herbs before the numbered stars. Those context lists are recorded below but are not added as star rows.

source_context_before_roster.sign_herbs_paraphrase: The text assigns Sange, two Vervine forms, Comfrey, Sowbread, Calamint, Mug-wort, Scorpion-grass, Pimpernell, Dock, Dragon-wort and Hart-wort to the twelve signs.
source_context_before_roster.planet_herbs_paraphrase: It gives one planetary list (including Sen-green, Agrimony, Sulphur-wort, Marygold, Wound-wort, Mulleine and Peony) and then an alternative Hermes/Albertus list (including Daffodill, Henbane, Rib-wort, Knotgrass, Vervine, Cinquefoile and Goos-foot).

plants.source_text: Suc-cory, whose leaves, and Flowers turn towards the North
plants.source_text_wikisource_variant: Succory, whose leaves, and Flowers turn towards the North
plants.qualification: directional description, not a plant-part identity

plants.ambiguity: common name retained; no modern species selected

PLANT_IDENTITY.rule: Merge only the explicitly permitted identity cases: Suc-cory/Succory, flowers of Perwinckle/Perwinkle, and Mandrake/the root of Mandrake. Remove the North-facing clause as description, not plant part. Retain all other historical names without modern botanical identification.
explicit_ambiguities: Bur and Quadraginus remain unresolved common/printed names.
No modern species or translation is supplied for any roster identity.

MATERIAL.rule: Keep part-qualified material names distinct, while treating Suc-cory/Succory and its North-facing clause as one Succory entry. Thus Mandrake differs from the root of Mandrake, and Perwinkle differs from flowers of Perwinckle.

repetition_and_source_limits.post_roster_source_qualification: The next paragraph says that a plant, stone or animal may receive influence from many stars conjointly, then gives multiple-star examples for stones and vegetables. Therefore repeated plant rows are source-compatible and are not an exclusive one-star dictionary.
repetition_and_source_limits.model_warning: A GDT960 requirement that each named plant/material maps to one unique whole Voynich group is a fixed target hypothesis; it is not entailed by the source's many-star qualification.
repetition_and_source_limits.identity_warning: PLANT_IDENTITY and MATERIAL are explicit rival normalizations. Neither is a modern botanical identification or a confirmed Voynich meaning.
